title: The trust region subproblem with non-intersecting linear constraints
contribution: Proves that the SDP + SOC-RLT + RLT relaxation of the trust-region subproblem with m linear cuts is exact for any m when no two cuts intersect inside the ball, giving with Burer-Anstreicher a two-sided demarcation of exactness.
problem_entry: Known exactness for m=0,1 and parallel m=2 plus the Burer-Anstreicher counterexample with cuts intersecting inside the ball left the non-intersecting case open (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Show every extreme point of F(Rm) is rank-1 by induction on m, splitting into a redundant-cut case and active SOC-RLT / tight RLT subcases (pp. 7-10).
assumptions: F(Tm) nonempty; Assumption 1: no two cut hyperplanes meet in F(Tm), checkable by convex feasibility problems (p. 6); relaxed to boundary intersections in Assumption 3 (p. 10).
proof_devices: Lemma 2: slack in cut i maps (x,X) to a feasible z_i via the SOC-RLT row (p. 6)
Lemma 3: an extreme point of a compact convex set intersected with a half-space is a combination of at most two extreme points (pp. 6-7)
induction on m with base case stated as m = 0 (p. 7), later corrected to m = 1 in S024 p. 21
SOC boundary-ray argument when an SOC-RLT row is active (Prop. 1, p. 8)
Schur complement on W = [s t I]^T Y [s t I] to rule out rank 2 (Prop. 2, pp. 9-10)
epsilon-shrunk ball and limit by compactness (Prop. 3, p. 11)
experiments: none as a study; numerical re-examination of the Burer-Anstreicher counterexample (p. 10) and an inscribed-pentagon example with numerical rank checks (pp. 11-12).
positioning: Builds on Sturm-Zhang, Ye-Zhang and Burer-Anstreicher; shows Ye-Zhang's multi-step method already extends for m=2 and claims novelty only for general m (pp. 2-4).
writing: Short 12-page paper: rival-analysis motivation section, three lemmas, two theorems leading to a corollary, counterexample re-read through the proof, one worked extension (pp. 3-12).
limits_future: Relies on Assumption 1 via Lemma 4 (p. 10); extension only to boundary intersections (p. 10); no future directions listed.

transferable: Prove relaxation exactness as 'every extreme point is rank-1' by induction on the number of added constraints, capping rank at 2 with the half-space lemma and ruling out rank 2 by a Schur complement (pp. 6-10).
Map a relaxation point with slack in a cut to a feasible original point read off the SOC-RLT row (Lemma 2, p. 6).
Re-examine the known counterexample against the proof step it breaks (p. 10).

quotes.text: This paper shows that the convex relaxation has no gap for arbitrary m as long as the linear constraints are non-intersecting.
On the other hand, we could not see how to extend the approach of Ye and Zhang to general m, and so to the best of our knowledge, our general approach in this paper contributes something new.

title: A gentle, geometric introduction to copositive optimization
contribution: A unified easiest-to-hardest tutorial deriving explicit convex hulls conv{(x,xx^T)} for intervals, triangles, quadrilaterals, balls, balls without non-intersecting caps, inscribed polygons and polytopes (via CP), plus a new conjectured cut class for general polygons backed by 6,000 random instances.
problem_entry: Entry by feasible-set geometry with few variables or constraints, aiming to characterize all cuts for each shape (pp. 2, 5).
key_idea: Homogenize, characterize K = conv{yy^T : y in cone} by PSD plus RLT/SOC-RLT constraints, dehomogenize via nu_k > 0; new partially-inscribed quadratic cuts for general polygons (pp. 7-8, 27-28).
assumptions: Proper (bounded, with interior) polygons; Lemma 2 DNN=CP only for d<=4, so no verbatim extension to simplices in R^4 (p. 8); non-intersecting non-redundant caps (Condition 1, p. 18); bounded polytope for CP (p. 30).
proof_devices: Maxfield-Minc DNN=CP for d<=4 with invertible C=(b,-A) (Prop. 1, p. 7)
augment C to an invertible C-hat with Y44=0 and project (Prop. 2, p. 11)
extreme-ray rank-1 by subtracting epsilon zz^T (Prop. 3, pp. 13-14)
three-case extreme-ray argument for one cap (Prop. 4, p. 16)
Lemma 5 half-space extreme rays plus Schur complement induction over caps (pp. 19-21)
dehomogenization nu_k > 0 reused across theorems (pp. 8, 14, 31)
lambda_max closed form for partially inscribed quadratics (p. 27)
experiments: Sec. 9: 6,000 random polygons (m=5..10, 1,000 each); 4,835 not rank-1 under PSD+CYC^T>=0; all solved after separating the new quadratics, 85% with 1-2 cuts, max 10 (pp. 28-29); solver and code not reported in the text.
positioning: Self-described unified presentation of Anstreicher-Burer, Sturm-Zhang, Burer-Anstreicher, Burer-Yang, Yang-Burer with simplified proofs; explicitly no comparison with B&B, sparsity or lifting hierarchies (p. 3); corrects the base case of Burer-Yang (p. 21).
writing: Scope disclaimer up front, easiest-to-hardest ordering, notation-reuse warning, one figure per geometry, short practice-oriented conclusion (pp. 3, 31-32).
limits_future: No proof that the Sec. 9 quadratics suffice (conjecture, p. 28); separation not claimed efficient (pp. 28-29); two-ellipsoid hull needs a semi-infinite family (p. 26); future: apply cut classes when the geometry appears as a substructure (pp. 31-32).

quotes.text: Hence, our main contribution is a unified presentation of the various results, and we do so from “easiest to hardest” in hopes of gently introducing the reader to the insights provided by copositive optimization.
At this time, we do not have a proof that all valid quadratics of the type described are enough to capture G, but we conjecture that they are.

title: A copositive approach for two-stage adjustable robust optimization with uncertain right-hand sides
contribution: Reformulates two-stage adjustable robust LP with uncertain right-hand sides exactly as a copositive program, shows the affine policy is a specific inner approximation of it, and derives SDP-based bounds between the two that are exact on a temporal-network family where the affine gap is unbounded.
problem_entry: ARO is NP-hard and the affine policy is the suboptimal tractable incumbent; after LP duality the worst-case recourse is a bilinear program with a known copositive representation (pp. 1-2, 6).
key_idea: Copositive representation of the inner max plus a redundant ball for Slater, dualize and collapse to one copositive minimization; the affine policy equals an inner approximation IA, so any in-between cone IB gives v_RLP <= v_IB <= v_Aff (pp. 6-12).
assumptions: Tractable X and full-dimensional cone U-hat, feasibility, boundedness, relatively complete recourse (Assumptions 1-4, p. 3); without Assumption 4 the program is still a valid upper bound (pp. 4, 8).
proof_devices: LP duality to a bilinear max over U x W (p. 6)
homogenization u1=1 and ZE^T=0 copositive representation (pp. 6-7)
redundant norm bound from polynomially bounded vertices of W gives Slater (pp. 7-8)
term-by-term sign check IA subset of COP (Lemma 1, pp. 10-11)
explicit dual certificate with PSD-on-null-space lemma and sum-of-squares completion (Prop. 6, Lemma 3, pp. 26-29)
rho -> 0 limit (Thm. 4, p. 16)
explicit optimal primal Z (Prop. 7, pp. 17, 29)
monotonicity in the uncertainty set (Prop. 8, pp. 29-30)
experiments: Mosek 8.0.0.28 beta via YALMIP/MATLAB R2014a, Intel i3 (p. 13); newsvendor IB -411.08 vs Aff -41.83 vs RLP -825.83 (p. 18); lot-sizing IB 1794.0 vs Aff 1950.8, LB 1573.8, no gain on the budget set (pp. 19-20); 1,000 random instances: 971 no gain, 29 close 20.2% on average (pp. 20-21); sizes and times 0.23-35 s (p. 21).
positioning: Affine, extended affine, polynomial policies, Ardestani-Jaafari-Delage, Chang et al.; prefers own approach for separating conic duality from the approximation choice; discloses the same-day equivalent result of Hanasusanto-Kuhn (pp. 2, 4-5).
writing: Roadmap framed by two extremes with interpolating approximations (p. 4); certificates relegated to the appendix (pp. 25-30); precise hedges such as 'we have not proved this formally' (p. 18); value of v_RLP,1 inconsistent between p. 14 and p. 17.
limits_future: No gain on the budget set and on 971/1,000 random instances (pp. 20-21); Assumption 4 unknown for the generator (p. 20); open: which policy class the copositive approach enforces and how to extract y(.) (p. 21).

title: Exact semidefinite formulations for a class of (random and non-random) nonconvex quadratic programs
contribution: Gives an LP-checkable data-dependent rank bound n-f+1 for Shor relaxations of diagonal QCQPs, eigenvalue-only exactness conditions for general QCQPs via a diagonalizing lift, and a high-probability exactness theorem for random QCQPs (arXiv v2 text; Theorem 3 later corrected per SKILL.md).
problem_entry: Data-free (Pataki/Barvinok) and tree-width (Laurent-Varvitsiotis, r*<=2 for diagonal) rank bounds cannot certify r*=1; the paper adds data dependence and average-case random analysis (pp. 2-5).
key_idea: Complementarity rank(Y*)+rank(Z*)<=n+1 and a feasibility number f from n Farkas LP systems give rank(Y*)<=n-f+1; general QCQPs are lifted to diagonal form via y_i=Q_i^T x (pp. 6-7, 13).
assumptions: Feasible; some ybar<=0 with sum ybar_i A_i negative definite (bounded); Slater interior (p. 6); Theorem 3 needs C PSD, Gaussian eigenvalues of A_i, an added ball, m<=n^q (p. 15).
proof_devices: Schur complement: S_jj=0 forces s_j=0, so rank(Z)>=f (Lemma 1, p. 7)
complementary rank bound (p. 6)
Farkas conversion of dual sign conditions into n LP systems (p. 7)
perturb-and-limit on objective data (pp. 9, 10, 12, 14, 17)
diagonalizing eigen-lift with a redundant ball (p. 13)
basis counting with C(n-1,2) bases, positive-probability open set, independence product theta^{nm} (pp. 16-17)
l'Hopital limit lemma (Lemma 3, p. 15)
experiments: none beyond a Monte Carlo estimate alpha ~ 1/6 (p. 17); analytic examples: knapsack where the bound is worse (p. 8), 2-norm/inf-norm ball intersection (p. 10), A_i in {+-I,0} (pp. 11-12).
positioning: Complements and refines Sojoudi-Lavaei (uses diagonal data they ignore) and gives a simplified derivation of Madani et al.'s r*<=2; distinguishes random-data analysis from smoothed analysis (pp. 4-5, 11, 13).
writing: Priority claim in the abstract (p. 1); honest example where the bound is worse (p. 8); closes with a conjecture and a suggested work-around (p. 17); credits the finder of the knapsack-example error (pp. 17-18).
limits_future: Bound can be weaker than the tree-width bound (p. 8); Theorem 2 drops linear terms (p. 14); random-C case conjectured, proof breaks for the X_jj system (p. 17); Theorem 3 later corrected (per SKILL.md, correction not read).
